- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often over-anticipates correction; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent peak) and under-estimates sustained rallies; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from forecasted peak values.
- In high-sentiment environments, model shows mean-reversion bias — over-predicts decline after rally; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counteract mean-reversion pressure.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently under-forecasts true price in 2024 Q4 (post-2024-10-10), especially when sentiment is volatile; apply a “volatility buffer” of +1–2% to forecast in such periods.
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., +0.5, -1.0, +0.5), model tends to “smooth” extremes; increase forecast volatility by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
